question: What is the total budget of {campaign_type} campaigns?
judge: A single total budget figure for campaigns of the named type.
rationale: Filter campaigns to the given campaign_type, ROUND(SUM(budget_amount), 2). Campaigns with a NULL budget contribute nothing.

question: How many campaigns are in the {campaign_status} state?
judge: A single count of campaigns in the named status.
rationale: Filter campaigns to the given status and count rows.

question: How many support cases are logged at {priority} priority?
judge: A single count of support cases at the named priority.
rationale: Filter support_cases to the given priority and count rows, boundary-date cases included.

question: How many support cases fall under {category}?
judge: A single count of support cases in the named category.
rationale: Filter support_cases to the given category and count rows.

question: How many interactions are {engagement_type} events?
judge: A single count of interactions of the named engagement type.
rationale: Filter interactions to the given engagement_type and count rows.

question: How many accounts do we have in the {region} region?
judge: A single count of accounts in the named region.
rationale: Filter accounts to the given region and count rows.

question: How many {priority}-priority support cases were resolved within their SLA deadline?
judge: A single count of resolved support cases at the named priority whose resolution time was on or before the SLA deadline. Unresolved cases do not count.
rationale: Filter support_cases to the given priority. A case is within SLA when resolved_at IS NOT NULL AND resolved_at <= sla_due_at. Count those rows.

question: How many support cases belong to {region}-region accounts?
judge: A single count of support cases whose owning account is in the named region.
rationale: INNER JOIN support_cases to accounts on account_id, filter to the region, count cases.

question: Which customer tier has the most {priority}-priority support cases?
judge: A single customer tier and its count of support cases at the named priority.
rationale: INNER JOIN support_cases to accounts, filter to the priority, count cases by customer_tier, order desc with customer_tier tie-break, top row.

question: How many contacts do we have across accounts in {industry}?
judge: A single count of contacts belonging to accounts in the named industry.
rationale: INNER JOIN contacts to accounts on account_id, filter to the industry, count contacts. Unassigned contacts (NULL account_id) are excluded by the INNER JOIN.

question: How many interactions are attributed to {campaign_type} campaigns?
judge: A single count of interactions attributed to campaigns of the named type.
rationale: INNER JOIN interactions to campaigns on campaign_id, filter to the type, count interactions. Organic interactions (NULL campaign_id) are excluded.

question: What is the inbound / outbound interaction breakdown for {is_active} contacts?
judge: Interactions split by direction (Inbound / Outbound) with counts, restricted to contacts matching the active flag.
rationale: INNER JOIN interactions to contacts on contact_id, filter to the is_active value, group by direction, order desc with direction tie-break.

question: Which accounts had the most {engagement_type} interactions recorded directly against them?
judge: Top accounts by count of the named engagement type on the direct account-to-interaction relationship, highest first.
rationale: INNER JOIN accounts to interactions on account_id (the nullable direct path), filter to the engagement_type, count by account, order desc with account_name tie-break, top 5.

question: How many {channel} interactions came from contacts with the title {title}?
judge: A single count of interactions on the named channel tied to contacts holding the named title.
rationale: INNER JOIN interactions to contacts on contact_id, filter to the channel and title, count interactions.

question: What percentage of support cases for accounts in {industry} were resolved within their SLA deadline?
judge: A single percentage (0-100, two decimals): of all support cases for accounts in the named industry, the share resolved on or before their SLA deadline. Unresolved cases count against the rate.
rationale: INNER JOIN support_cases to accounts on account_id, filter to the industry. A case is within SLA when resolved_at IS NOT NULL AND resolved_at <= sla_due_at. Rate = 100.0 * within-SLA count / total case count, rounded to 2 places.

question: How many {region}-region accounts have no contacts on record?
judge: A single count of accounts in the named region with zero associated contacts.
rationale: LEFT JOIN accounts to contacts on account_id, filter accounts to the region, keep rows where contact_id IS NULL, count.

question: How many accounts in {industry} have no contacts on record?
judge: A single count of accounts in the named industry with zero associated contacts.
rationale: LEFT JOIN accounts to contacts on account_id, filter accounts to the industry, keep rows where contact_id IS NULL, count.

question: How many contacts with the title {title} have no recorded interactions?
judge: A single count of contacts holding the named title that have zero interactions.
rationale: LEFT JOIN contacts to interactions on contact_id, filter contacts to the title, keep rows where interaction_id IS NULL, count.

question: How many contacts with the title {title} are not enrolled in any campaign?
judge: A single count of contacts holding the named title with no campaign membership row.
rationale: LEFT JOIN contacts to contact_campaigns on contact_id, filter contacts to the title, keep rows where campaign_id IS NULL, count.

question: How many {campaign_type} campaigns have no attributed interactions?
judge: A single count of campaigns of the named type with zero attributed interactions.
rationale: LEFT JOIN campaigns to interactions on campaign_id, filter campaigns to the type, keep rows where interaction_id IS NULL, count.

question: How many {campaign_status} campaigns have no attributed interactions?
judge: A single count of campaigns in the named status with zero attributed interactions.
rationale: LEFT JOIN campaigns to interactions on campaign_id, filter campaigns to the status, keep rows where interaction_id IS NULL, count.

question: For {region}-region accounts, how does engagement break down by interaction channel?
fields: accounts.account_id, accounts.region, contacts.account_id, contacts.contact_id, interactions.contact_id, interactions.channel, interactions.engagement_points
judge: Interaction channels ranked by total engagement_points, restricted to interactions of contacts whose account is in the named region, highest first, with totals.
rationale: INNER JOIN accounts -> contacts -> interactions, filter to the region, GROUP BY channel, SUM(engagement_points), order desc with channel tie-break.

question: For accounts in {industry}, how do the support cases raised by their contacts break down by priority?
fields: accounts.account_id, accounts.industry, contacts.account_id, contacts.contact_id, support_cases.contact_id, support_cases.priority, support_cases.case_id
judge: Support-case priorities ranked by count, restricted to cases whose requesting contact belongs to an account in the named industry, highest first.
rationale: INNER JOIN accounts -> contacts -> support_cases, filter to the industry, GROUP BY priority, count cases, order desc with priority tie-break. Account-level cases (NULL contact_id) are excluded.

question: For {customer_tier}-tier accounts, what is the SLA compliance rate of the support cases raised by their contacts, by category?
fields: accounts.account_id, accounts.customer_tier, contacts.account_id, contacts.contact_id, support_cases.contact_id, support_cases.category, support_cases.resolved_at, support_cases.sla_due_at
judge: For each support-case category, the percentage (0-100, two decimals) of cases resolved on or before the SLA deadline, restricted to cases whose contact belongs to an account in the named tier. Categories listed alphabetically.
rationale: INNER JOIN accounts -> contacts -> support_cases, filter to the tier, GROUP BY category. Within-SLA = resolved_at IS NOT NULL AND resolved_at <= sla_due_at. Rate = 100.0 * within-SLA / total per category, 2 places, ordered by category.

question: For {campaign_type} campaigns, which contact titles carry the most multi-touch attribution weight?
fields: contacts.contact_id, contacts.title, contact_campaigns.contact_id, contact_campaigns.campaign_id, contact_campaigns.attribution_weight, campaigns.campaign_id, campaigns.campaign_type
judge: Contact titles ranked by summed attribution_weight for memberships of campaigns of the named type, four decimals, highest first. Memberships whose attribution_weight is missing contribute nothing.
rationale: INNER JOIN contacts -> contact_campaigns -> campaigns (all three essential: contacts supplies the grouping title, contact_campaigns the weight, campaigns the filter). Filter to the campaign_type, GROUP BY contacts.title, ROUND(SUM(contact_campaigns.attribution_weight), 4). Rows with a NULL attribution_weight (the ~2.5% missing-value imperfection) are skipped by SUM - the declared NULL handling for this measure. Order desc with title tie-break.

question: For {region}-region accounts, how do the support cases raised by their contacts break down by status?
fields: accounts.account_id, accounts.region, contacts.account_id, contacts.contact_id, support_cases.contact_id, support_cases.status, support_cases.case_id
judge: Support-case statuses ranked by count, restricted to cases whose requesting contact belongs to an account in the named region, highest first.
rationale: INNER JOIN accounts -> contacts -> support_cases, filter to the region, GROUP BY status, count cases, order desc with status tie-break.

question: For accounts in {industry}, how does engagement break down by interaction type?
fields: accounts.account_id, accounts.industry, contacts.account_id, contacts.contact_id, interactions.contact_id, interactions.engagement_type, interactions.engagement_points
judge: Interaction engagement types ranked by total engagement_points, restricted to interactions of contacts whose account is in the named industry, highest first.
rationale: INNER JOIN accounts -> contacts -> interactions, filter to the industry, GROUP BY engagement_type, SUM(engagement_points), order desc with engagement_type tie-break.

question: Which three campaign types drove the most engagement among {region}-region accounts?
fields: campaigns.campaign_id, campaigns.campaign_type, interactions.campaign_id, interactions.contact_id, interactions.engagement_points, contacts.contact_id, contacts.account_id, accounts.account_id, accounts.region
judge: Exactly three campaign types ranked by total engagement_points among accounts in the named region, highest first, with totals.
rationale: Join campaigns -> interactions -> contacts -> accounts, filter to the region, SUM(engagement_points) per campaign_type, order desc with campaign_type tie-break, top 3.

question: Which accounts have the largest open backlog of {category} support cases right now?
fields: accounts.account_id, accounts.account_name, support_cases.account_id, support_cases.category, support_cases.status, support_cases.case_id
judge: Top accounts by count of unresolved support cases in the named category, highest first.
rationale: INNER JOIN accounts to support_cases on account_id, filter to the category and unresolved statuses, count by account, order desc with account_name tie-break, top 5.

question: Which accounts in {industry} look at risk from an open support backlog and no recent engagement?
fields: accounts.account_id, accounts.account_name, accounts.industry, support_cases.account_id, support_cases.status, interactions.contact_id, interactions.interaction_at, contacts.contact_id, contacts.account_id
judge: Accounts in the named industry with at least three unresolved support cases and zero interactions (via their contacts) in the 60 days before the reference date, with the two supporting numbers.
rationale: Count unresolved cases per account and interactions since 2026-06-02 (60 days before reference_today 2026-08-01) attributed through the contact's account. Filter to the industry, >= 3 open cases, 0 recent interactions, order by open-case count desc with account_name tie-break, top 5.

question: How did engagement among {region}-region accounts change from Q1 2026 to Q2 2026?
fields: interactions.contact_id, interactions.interaction_at, interactions.engagement_points, contacts.contact_id, contacts.account_id, accounts.account_id, accounts.region
judge: Total engagement_points for Q1 2026 and Q2 2026 for the named region, the absolute and percentage change, and the direction. Q1 and Q2 are the two most recent complete calendar quarters relative to the reference date 2026-08-01.
rationale: Q1 2026 = 2026-01-01..2026-04-01, Q2 2026 = 2026-04-01..2026-07-01 - the two most recent COMPLETE quarters (data ends 2026-07-28, so Q3 is excluded). INNER JOIN interactions -> contacts -> accounts, filter to the region, SUM(engagement_points) per window, then compute absolute and percentage change and direction.

question: Which region had the best engagement trend among {customer_tier}-tier accounts from Q1 2026 to Q2 2026?
fields: accounts.account_id, accounts.region, accounts.customer_tier, contacts.account_id, contacts.contact_id, interactions.contact_id, interactions.engagement_points, interactions.interaction_at
judge: The single region with the highest percentage change in engagement_points from Q1 2026 to Q2 2026 among accounts in the named customer tier - the largest gain, or (if every region declined) the smallest decline. Regions with zero Q1 engagement are excluded.
rationale: Q1 2026 = 2026-01-01..2026-04-01, Q2 2026 = 2026-04-01..2026-07-01 (the two most recent COMPLETE quarters; data ends 2026-07-28). INNER JOIN accounts -> contacts -> interactions, restrict to the tier, SUM(engagement_points) per region per window. pct_change = (Q2 - Q1) / Q1 * 100. Regions with zero Q1 are undefined and sorted last. Take the region with the highest pct_change (does NOT assume growth).
